page: Google Cloud Platform z4d-highmem-32-standardlssd is a member of the z4d server family, configured with 32 dedicated vCPUs on the x86_64 architecture. It features 252.0 GB of system memory, yielding approximately 7.88 GB of RAM per core. While the local storage size is specified as None in the configuration payload, the system is associated with NVMe SSD storage types. There are no complimentary public IPv4 addresses included with this instance, and it does not feature any GPU acceleration.

With a memory-to-vCPU ratio of nearly 1:8, this server type is positioned for memory-intensive workloads. The dedicated CPU allocation ensures consistent processing performance without the resource contention typical of shared-core instances. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the high memory density per vCPU provides a specialized resource profile that reduces the need to scale up to larger, more expensive instances simply to meet memory capacity requirements.

This configuration is suitable for memory-intensive applications, database caching layers, and enterprise workloads requiring substantial RAM capacity alongside moderate compute power. The lack of integrated GPU accelerators makes it unsuitable for hardware-accelerated machine learning training, while the dedicated x86_64 cores support standard enterprise software stacks and relational database management systems.
